control-action-sheet-action.summary: One choice in an [`action_sheet`](/docs/control-action-sheet). Give its label as the first argument or as `content:`, a string or a control; `default: true` shows it in bold and `destructive: true` in red. Tapping it fires `on_click` and does not close the sheet, so close the sheet in the handler. On iOS and macOS it is an iOS action sheet button; on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a list row, which ignores the common layout properties and dims while `disabled`.
example: cancel: action_sheet_action("Keep it", default: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.close_bottom_sheet(sheet) })

control-arc.summary: Part of an ellipse, from `start_angle` for `sweep_angle` radians, drawn as a curve or, with `use_center`, a pie slice. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: arc(x: 10, y: 10, width: 100, height: 100, start_angle: 0, sweep_angle: 2 * Math::PI,
arc(x: 10, y: 10, width: 100, height: 100, start_angle: -Math::PI / 2, sweep_angle: 2 * Math::PI * progress,
arc(x: 140, y: 10, width: 100, height: 100, start_angle: 0, sweep_angle: Math::PI / 2, use_center: true,

control-audio.summary: Plays a sound or a music track from a URL, an asset or base64 data. It is a page service, not a visible control: create it with `page.audio(...)`, keep the object and call `play`, `pause` or `seek` on it; build your own buttons and read the position and state from its events. It works on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web. Part of the [`audio` extension](/docs/extension-audio): add `audio` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-banner-ad.summary: A Google Mobile Ads (AdMob) banner, 320 by 50 logical pixels, on Android and iOS. Always set `unit_id`: without it the client falls back to Google's interstitial test ids (a client bug), so no test banner shows. Google's banner test units are `ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/6300978111` on Android and `ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/2934735716` on iOS; use your own unit id, and your own AdMob app, before you ship. On other platforms the ad does not load. Part of the [`ads` extension](/docs/extension-ads): add `ads` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: # Google's banner test units. Use your own unit ids before you ship.
unit_id: test_units[:android], # test_units[:ios] in an iOS build

control-bar-chart.summary: A bar chart drawn with fl_chart. Put one [`bar_chart_group`](/docs/control-bar-chart-group) per x position in `groups`, and the bars of each group in its `rods`. Add [`chart_axis`](/docs/control-chart-axis) for labels and `on_event` to react to touches. It looks the same on every platform. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: bar_chart_group(x: index, rods: [bar_chart_rod(to_y: amount, width: 22, color: "#2563eb", border_radius: 4)])
bottom_axis: chart_axis(labels: months.each_with_index.map { |name, index| chart_axis_label(value: index, label: name) }),

control-bar-chart-group.summary: The bars at one x position of a [`bar_chart`](/docs/control-bar-chart), side by side or, with `group_vertically: true`, on top of each other. It is not drawn on its own: put it in the chart's `groups`. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-bar-chart-rod.summary: One bar of a [`bar_chart_group`](/docs/control-bar-chart-group), from `from_y` to `to_y`, with an optional track behind it and stacked segments inside it. Update it like any control, for example `page.update(rod, to_y: 80)`. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release, `tooltip:` (a text, or a hash with `text` and `text_style`) replaces the value in the bar's touch bubble. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: gradient: { _type: "linear", begin: { x: 0, y: 1 }, end: { x: 0, y: -1 }, colors: ["#93c5fd", "#1d4ed8"] },

control-bar-chart-rod-stack-item.summary: A segment inside a [`bar_chart_rod`](/docs/control-bar-chart-rod), for stacked bars. Give every segment `from_y`, `to_y` and `color`, and make them cover the rod's range. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: bar_chart_rod_stack_item(from_y: 70, to_y: 90, color: "#dc2626", border_side: { color: "#7f1d1d", width: 1 })

control-block-picker.summary: A grid of color swatches; the user taps one to pick it. iOS and macOS draw Cupertino-styled swatches. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. Changing `color` from Ruby after the picker is shown moves the selection only with the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-candlestick-chart.summary: A candlestick (OHLC) chart for prices drawn with fl_chart: one candle per [`candlestick_chart_spot`](/docs/control-candlestick-chart-spot). With 0.0.23 it shows no touch bubble, so use `on_event` to show the touched candle. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release a candle with its own `tooltip:` text shows it in a bubble. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: spots: prices.map { |x, open, high, low, close| candlestick_chart_spot(x: x, open: open, high: high, low: low, close: close) },
page.update(status, value: "Day #{index}: closed at #{prices[index][4]}") if index

control-candlestick-chart-spot.summary: One candle of a [`candlestick_chart`](/docs/control-candlestick-chart): the `open`, `high`, `low` and `close` prices at `x`. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release, `tooltip:` (a text, or a hash with `text` and `text_style`) gives the candle a touch bubble; with 0.0.23 candlestick charts show none. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-canvas.summary: A drawing surface that paints a list of shapes: lines, circles, arcs, ovals, rectangles, paths, points and shadows. Change a shape with `page.update(shape, ...)`, or replace them all with `page.update(canvas, shapes: [...])`. Put a `gesture_detector` in `content` to draw with the finger. It is core Ruflet and looks the same on every platform.
example: sky = rect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 320, height: 200, paint: paint(color: "#bfdbfe"))
sun = circle(x: 260, y: 50, radius: 28, paint: paint(color: "#facc15"))
elements: [path_move_to(0, 200), path_quadratic_to(cp1x: 160, cp1y: 60, x: 320, y: 200, w: 1), path_close],
page.add(button("Sunset", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sun, y: 150, paint: paint(color: "#f97316")) }))

control-chart-axis.summary: The labels and title along one side of a bar, line, scatter or candlestick chart. Pass it as `left_axis`, `right_axis`, `top_axis` or `bottom_axis`; a side without an axis shows no labels. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: left_axis: chart_axis(title: text(value: "Temperature (C)"), title_size: 24, label_size: 32, label_spacing: 10),
bottom_axis: chart_axis(label_spacing: 1, show_min: false, show_max: false),

control-chart-axis-label.summary: A custom label at one value of a [`chart_axis`](/docs/control-chart-axis), such as a month name under a bar. The label is drawn only when its `value` is one of the axis ticks. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: groups: [6, 8, 5, 9, 7].each_with_index.map { |hours, x| bar_chart_group(x: x, rods: [bar_chart_rod(to_y: hours, width: 16)]) },
chart_axis_label(value: x, label: x == 3 ? text(value: day, weight: "bold", color: "#dc2626") : day)

control-circle.summary: A circle around the point `x`, `y`. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: circle(x: 60, y: 60, radius: 50, paint: paint(color: "#b45309", style: "stroke", stroke_width: 3, stroke_dash_pattern: [8, 4]))

control-circle-layer.summary: The layer of a [`map`](/docs/control-map) that draws [`circle_marker`](/docs/control-circle-marker) controls. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: circle_marker(coordinates: [lat, lng], radius: bikes, color: "#16a34a,0.6", border_color: "#14532d", border_stroke_width: 1)

control-circle-marker.summary: A circle on the map, sized in pixels or, with `use_radius_in_meter`, in meters on the ground, for example a coverage area. Put it in a [`circle_layer`](/docs/control-circle-layer). Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-color.summary: Fills the whole canvas with one color, for a background or a tint. Build it with `canvas_color(...)` or `color(...)`. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.

control-color-picker.summary: A full color picker: a color area with hue and transparency sliders, value fields and an optional history of recent colors. `on_color_change` reports the pick. iOS and macOS draw it with Cupertino-styled parts. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release the client also writes the pick back to `color`, so `event.control.props["color"]` stays current; with 0.0.23 read it from `event.data`. A `color` you change from Ruby after the user has picked also moves the selection only with the next release: on 0.0.23 the pick sets `hsv_color`, which then wins. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-cupertino-action-sheet.summary: The `cupertino_action_sheet` spelling of [`action_sheet`](/docs/control-action-sheet): a title, a message, a list of choices and a separate Cancel choice. It sends the same `ActionSheet` control, so the client draws it by platform: an iOS action sheet on iOS and macOS, and a column of list rows on Android, web, Windows and Linux. Present it in a bottom sheet with `page.show_bottom_sheet`, and build its choices with [`cupertino_action_sheet_action`](/docs/control-cupertino-action-sheet-action). With 0.0.23 the iOS action sheet floats over the dimmed page; with the next release the bottom sheet draws it on its own panel with rounded top corners, in the sheet's `bgcolor`. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: cancel: cupertino_action_sheet_action(content: "Cancel", default: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.close_bottom_sheet(sheet) })

control-cupertino-action-sheet-action.summary: The `cupertino_action_sheet_action` spelling of [`action_sheet_action`](/docs/control-action-sheet-action), one choice in a [`cupertino_action_sheet`](/docs/control-cupertino-action-sheet). It takes keyword arguments only, so pass the label as `content:`. It sends the same `ActionSheetAction` control and behaves the same way: `default:` and `destructive:` style it, and `on_click` fires without closing the sheet.

control-cupertino-activity-indicator.summary: The iOS spinner: spokes that turn while `animating` is true (the default), sized by `radius` (default 10). `progress`, from 0.0 to 1.0, shows only part of the spokes instead. It sends the same `ProgressRing` control as [`progress_ring`](/docs/control-progress-ring), so Android, web, Windows and Linux draw a Material progress ring, which ignores `radius` and `animating`; there the 0.0.23 client also ignores `progress` and always spins. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-cupertino-alert-dialog.summary: The `cupertino_alert_dialog` spelling of [`alert_dialog`](/docs/control-alert-dialog). It sends the same `AlertDialog` control, so the client draws it by platform: an iOS alert on iOS and macOS and a Material dialog on Android, web, Windows and Linux. Besides the common properties it accepts only `title`, `content`, `actions`, `modal`, `barrier_color`, `inset_animation`, `open` and `on_dismiss`, and raises `ArgumentError` for any other keyword; use `alert_dialog` for the Material styling properties. Open it with `page.show_dialog` and close it with `page.close_dialog` in the buttons' handlers. On iOS and macOS the buttons become iOS dialog actions, and `button(..., default: true)` or `destructive: true` makes one bold or red.
example: content: text("Maps uses your location to show nearby places."),
page.add(column(children: [status, cupertino_button("Turn on location", on_click: ->(_event) { page.show_dialog(dialog) })]))

control-cupertino-bottom-sheet.summary: The `cupertino_bottom_sheet` spelling of [`bottom_sheet`](/docs/control-bottom-sheet), often used for a `picker`, `timer_picker`, `date_picker` or [`cupertino_action_sheet`](/docs/control-cupertino-action-sheet). It sends the same `BottomSheet` control, so it is an iOS popup sheet on iOS and macOS and a Material bottom sheet on Android, web, Windows and Linux. Show it with `page.show_bottom_sheet` and close it with `page.close_bottom_sheet`. On iOS and macOS, picker content sits on a fixed panel, 220 high unless you set `height`. With 0.0.23 `cupertino_bottom_sheet` raises `ArgumentError` for `dismissible`, `barrier_color`, `draggable`, `scrollable`, `fullscreen` and the other sizing properties, which `bottom_sheet` accepts. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: page.add(column(children: [choice, cupertino_button("Choose a size", on_click: ->(_event) { page.show_bottom_sheet(sheet) })]))

control-cupertino-date-picker.summary: An iOS-style wheel for picking a date, a time, or both. Open it with `page.show_dialog(picker)`: on iOS and macOS the wheel slides up with Cancel and Done, and on Android, web, Windows and Linux the client shows the Material date picker dialog. When the user confirms, `on_change` gets the picked moment in `event.data`, an ISO 8601 string in UTC. With 0.0.23 a picker added to the page shows nothing; drawing it in place with `page.add` (the wheel on iOS and macOS, a calendar elsewhere) needs the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-cupertino-list-tile.summary: The `cupertino_list_tile` spelling of [`list_tile`](/docs/control-list-tile). It sends the same `ListTile` control, so it is an iOS list row on iOS and macOS and a Material list row on Android, web, Windows and Linux. It accepts the properties of the iOS row: `title` (required), `subtitle`, `leading`, `trailing`, `additional_info`, `bgcolor`, `bgcolor_activated`, `notched`, `leading_size`, `leading_to_title`, `padding`, `toggle_inputs`, `url` and `on_click`; use `list_tile` for the Material-only properties. `additional_info`, `bgcolor_activated`, `notched`, `leading_size` and `leading_to_title` apply on iOS and macOS only. With 0.0.23 pad a row with `list_tile(content_padding: 16)`: `padding` takes effect only with the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-data-cell.summary: One cell of a [`data_table`](/docs/control-data-table) or [`data_table2`](/docs/control-data-table-2) row: `data_cell(content)` with a control, usually a `text`. A cell fires `on_tap`, `on_double_tap` and `on_long_press`; `on_tap_down` gives the touch point in `event.local_position`. `show_edit_icon: true` adds a pencil icon to show that tapping edits the value, and `placeholder: true` draws the content as placeholder text. In a `data_table` those two, `on_tap_down` and `on_tap_cancel` apply on Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
example: status = text("Tap a price to edit it")

control-data-column.summary: A column heading of a [`data_table`](/docs/control-data-table): `data_column(label)` with a string or a control. `numeric: true` right-aligns the column for numbers, `tooltip` explains the heading, and `on_sort` makes the heading sortable: `event.data[:ci]` is the column index. The table does not sort itself: reorder `rows` and set `sort_column_index` and `sort_ascending`. On iOS and macOS `numeric`, `heading_row_alignment` and `tooltip` have no effect, no sort arrow is drawn, and `event.data[:asc]` is the table's current `sort_ascending`, so keep the direction in Ruby.

control-data-column-2.summary: A column heading of a [`data_table2`](/docs/control-data-table-2) table, from the `datatable2` extension: `data_column2(label, size:, fixed_width:, numeric:, on_sort:)`. The table shares its width between the columns by `size`: `"s"` (default), `"m"` or `"l"`, weighted by the table's `sm_ratio` and `lm_ratio`. `fixed_width` gives a column an exact width instead. `on_sort` gets the column index in `event.data[:ci]` and the new direction in `event.data[:asc]` on every platform.

control-data-row.summary: A row of a [`data_table`](/docs/control-data-table): `data_row(cells)` with exactly one [`data_cell`](/docs/control-data-cell) per column. `color` sets its background and `selected` draws it as selected. With `on_select_change` and the table's `show_checkbox_column`, the row gets a checkbox: `event.data` is `true` when it is selected and `nil` when it is cleared, and the row does not change until you set `selected` with `page.update`. On iOS and macOS `on_long_press` is never sent, and the 0.0.23 client shows no checkbox and never sends `on_select_change`. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-data-row-2.summary: A row of a [`data_table2`](/docs/control-data-table-2) table, from the `datatable2` extension: `data_row2(cells)` with one [`data_cell`](/docs/control-data-cell) per column. On top of a `data_row`'s `color`, `selected` and `on_select_change`, a row can have its own height (`specific_row_height`) and box `decoration`, and it fires `on_tap`, `on_double_tap`, `on_long_press`, `on_secondary_tap` and `on_secondary_tap_down`, which gives the pointer position in `event.local_position` and `event.global_position`.
example: status = text("Tap or right-click a row")

control-expansion-panel.summary: One panel of an [`expansion_panel_list`](/docs/control-expansion-panel-list): a `header` row that stays visible and `content` shown below it while the panel is open (`expanded`). It takes keyword arguments only. The list fires `on_change` with the panel's index when the header is tapped; the panel itself has no events, and its common layout properties have no effect. `can_tap_header: true` lets the whole header toggle the panel on Android, web, Windows and Linux, where otherwise only the arrow does; on iOS and macOS the whole header always does, and the panel is redrawn only when Ruby updates the list.
example: content: list_tile(title: text("Orders ship within two working days.")),
content: list_tile(title: text("Return any item within 30 days.")),
list = expansion_panel_list(panels, on_change: ->(_event) { page.update(list, controls: panels) })

control-fill.summary: Fills the whole canvas with a `paint`, for example a gradient background. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: rect(x: 40, y: 40, width: 80, height: 40, border_radius: 8, paint: paint(color: "#ffffff"))

control-hue-ring-picker.summary: A ring of hues around a saturation and brightness square, a compact color picker. iOS and macOS draw it with Cupertino-styled parts. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-image-source-attribution.summary: A logo in a [`rich_attribution`](/docs/control-rich-attribution) that stays visible next to its button. It is drawn only there. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-interstitial-ad.summary: A full-screen Google Mobile Ads (AdMob) interstitial on Android and iOS. It is a page service, not a visible control: register it with `page.add_service(ad)`, wait for `on_load`, then call `ad.show`. A loaded ad can be shown once; register a new one for the next break. Without `unit_id` the client loads Google's test unit. Part of the [`ads` extension](/docs/extension-ads): add `ads` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-line.summary: A straight line from `x1`, `y1` to `x2`, `y2`. Give it a `paint` with `stroke_width`, or it is a hairline. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: line(x1: offset, y1: 0, x2: offset, y2: 160, paint: paint(color: "#d1d5db", stroke_width: 1)),
line(x1: 0, y1: offset, x2: 160, y2: offset, paint: paint(color: "#d1d5db", stroke_width: 1))
diagonal = line(x1: 0, y1: 160, x2: 160, y2: 0, paint: paint(color: "#dc2626", stroke_width: 3, stroke_dash_pattern: [10, 5]))

control-line-chart.summary: A line or area chart drawn with fl_chart. Each [`line_chart_data`](/docs/control-line-chart-data) in `data_series` is one line through its points. Touching shows the values under the finger, and `on_event` reports the touch. It looks the same on every platform. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release `event.data[:spots]` also says which points were touched; with 0.0.23 each of its entries is an empty String. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: points: readings.map { |x, y| line_chart_data_point(x: x, y: y) }
# With 0.0.23 the spots arrive as empty Strings, so only hashes are read.

control-line-chart-data.summary: One line of a [`line_chart`](/docs/control-line-chart): its points, color, thickness and the optional fill above or below it. Points have no dots unless you set `point`. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: planned = [[0, 2], [1, 3], [2, 4], [3, 5]].map { |x, y| line_chart_data_point(x: x, y: y) }
actual = [[0, 1.5], [1, 3.2], [2, 3.6], [3, 5.4]].map { |x, y| line_chart_data_point(x: x, y: y) }
below_line_gradient: { _type: "linear", begin: { x: 0, y: -1 }, end: { x: 0, y: 1 }, colors: ["#2563eb,0.3", "#2563eb,0.0"] }

control-line-chart-data-point.summary: One point of a [`line_chart_data`](/docs/control-line-chart-data) line, at `x` and `y`. Mark it `selected` to highlight it on a chart with `interactive: false`. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release, `tooltip:` (a text, or a hash with `text` and `text_style`) replaces the value in the point's touch bubble. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: line_chart_data_point(x: x, y: y, selected: y == 9)

control-lottie.summary: Plays a Lottie animation (an After Effects export in JSON) from a URL, an asset or base64 data. It loops by default; update `animate` to stop and start it. It looks the same on every platform. Part of the [`lottie` extension](/docs/extension-lottie): add `lottie` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With 0.0.23 a base64 `src` is decoded again on every update of the control, such as `animate: false`, so the animation loads again from its first frame and `on_load` fires again; the next release only applies the change. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-map.summary: An interactive map drawn with flutter_map. It shows its `layers` bottom to top: tiles from a [`tile_layer`](/docs/control-tile-layer), then markers, circles, lines, areas and an attribution. The user can pan, zoom and rotate it; tap events report map coordinates, and methods such as `move_to` and `zoom_in` move it from Ruby once it is on the page. It works the same on every platform. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: button("Back to Paris", on_click: ->(_event) { city_map.move_to(destination: paris, zoom: 12) })

control-marker.summary: A control pinned to a point of the map, such as an icon or a label. It moves with the map and keeps its size. Put it in a [`marker_layer`](/docs/control-marker-layer). Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: container(content: text(value: "HQ", color: "#ffffff"), bgcolor: "#1d4ed8", padding: 6, border_radius: 6),

control-marker-layer.summary: The layer of a [`map`](/docs/control-map) that draws [`marker`](/docs/control-marker) controls. Update its `markers` to add or remove pins. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: icon_button("storefront", icon_color: "#dc2626", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(selected, value: name) }),

control-material-picker.summary: Picks a color from the Material Design palette: first a hue, then one of its shades. iOS and macOS draw it with Cupertino-styled parts. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. Changing `color` from Ruby after the picker is shown moves the selection only with the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-multiple-choice-block-picker.summary: A grid of color swatches where the user can select several. iOS and macOS draw Cupertino-styled swatches. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. Changing `colors` from Ruby after the picker is shown updates the selection only with the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-native-ad.summary: A Google Mobile Ads native ad styled with a template or a native factory. The Ruby helper exists, but neither the 0.0.23 client nor the next release draws it yet: the `ads` extension does not register NativeAd, so the page shows an "Unknown control: NativeAd" box where you add it. Use [`banner_ad`](/docs/control-banner-ad) for now. Part of the [`ads` extension](/docs/extension-ads): add `ads` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-oval.summary: An ellipse that fills the box at `x`, `y` of `width` by `height`. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: oval(x: 10, y: 20, width: 140, height: 80, paint: paint(color: "#c7d2fe")),
oval(x: 10, y: 20, width: 140, height: 80, paint: paint(color: "#4338ca", style: "stroke", stroke_width: 2))

control-path.summary: A free-form outline built from drawing steps such as `path_move_to`, `path_line_to`, curves and `path_close`, then filled or stroked. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: elements: [path_move_to(130, 60), path_cubic_to(cp1x: 160, cp1y: 0, cp2x: 190, cp2y: 120, x: 220, y: 60)],

control-pie-chart.summary: A pie or donut chart drawn with fl_chart. Each [`pie_chart_section`](/docs/control-pie-chart-section) is a slice sized by its `value`. Unset, `center_space_radius` leaves a large hole: set `0` for a full pie. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: pie_chart_section(value: share, title: "#{share}%", color: colors[index], radius: 60,

control-pie-chart-section.summary: One slice of a [`pie_chart`](/docs/control-pie-chart), sized by `value` in proportion to the other slices, with an optional title and badge. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: pie_chart_section(value: 30, color: "#d1d5db", radius: 80, title: "Left", border_side: { color: "#ffffff", width: 2 })

control-points.summary: A set of points drawn as dots, as line pairs or as one connected outline. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: points(points: samples, point_mode: "polygon", paint: paint(color: "#94a3b8", stroke_width: 2)),
points(points: samples, point_mode: "points", paint: paint(color: "#0f172a", stroke_width: 8, stroke_cap: "round"))

control-polygon-layer.summary: The layer of a [`map`](/docs/control-map) that draws [`polygon_marker`](/docs/control-polygon-marker) areas. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: polygon_marker(coordinates: corners, label: name, color: "#7c3aed,0.25", border_color: "#7c3aed", border_stroke_width: 2)

control-polygon-marker.summary: A filled area on the map, such as a delivery zone, with an optional outline and label. Put it in a [`polygon_layer`](/docs/control-polygon-layer). Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-polyline-layer.summary: The layer of a [`map`](/docs/control-map) that draws [`polyline_marker`](/docs/control-polyline-marker) lines. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-polyline-marker.summary: A line through points on the map, such as a route or a border, solid, dotted, dashed or in a gradient. Put it in a [`polyline_layer`](/docs/control-polyline-layer). Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-popup-menu-item.summary: One entry in a [`popup_menu_button`](/docs/control-popup-menu-button) menu, with text, an icon, or both. Set `checked` for a check mark. The client does not change it, so keep the state yourself and update `checked` in `on_click`: `event.data` is `true` or `nil`, never `false`, and the 0.0.23 client on iOS and macOS sends none. Leave out both text and icon for a divider. Icons, check marks and dividers show on Android, web, Windows and Linux only: on iOS and macOS the menu shows each item's text and nothing else, and an item without text draws an error box.
example: popup_menu_item("Name", icon: "sort_by_alpha", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by name") }),
popup_menu_item("Date", icon: "event", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by date") }),

control-radar-chart.summary: A radar (spider) chart drawn with fl_chart that compares values along several spokes. Each [`radar_data_set`](/docs/control-radar-data-set) is one shape, and [`radar_chart_title`](/docs/control-radar-chart-title) labels the spokes. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-radar-chart-title.summary: The label of one spoke of a [`radar_chart`](/docs/control-radar-chart). Titles are matched to spokes by position. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-radar-data-set.summary: One shape on a [`radar_chart`](/docs/control-radar-chart): one value per spoke, with its fill and outline. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: titles: %w[Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri].map { |day| radar_chart_title(text: day) },

control-radar-data-set-entry.summary: One value of a [`radar_data_set`](/docs/control-radar-data-set), on the spoke at the same position. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-rect.summary: A rectangle at `x`, `y`, optionally with rounded corners. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.
example: rect(x: 10, y: 10, width: 140, height: 80, border_radius: 12, paint: paint(color: "#dcfce7")),
rect(x: 10, y: 10, width: 140, height: 80, border_radius: { top_left: 12, bottom_right: 12 },

control-rich-attribution.summary: An attribution button for a [`map`](/docs/control-map) that opens a popup listing every data source, with logos that stay visible. List the sources with [`text_source_attribution`](/docs/control-text-source-attribution) and [`image_source_attribution`](/docs/control-image-source-attribution). iOS and macOS draw a Cupertino popup. Put it last in the map's `layers`. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-scatter-chart.summary: A scatter chart drawn with fl_chart: one dot per [`scatter_chart_spot`](/docs/control-scatter-chart-spot), with optional labels. With 0.0.23 it shows no touch bubble, so use `on_event` to show the touched spot. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release a spot with its own `tooltip:` text shows it in a bubble. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: spots: cities.map { |name, x, y| scatter_chart_spot(x: x, y: y, radius: 8, color: "#0891b2", label_text: name) },

control-scatter-chart-spot.summary: One dot of a [`scatter_chart`](/docs/control-scatter-chart), at `x` and `y`, with its own size, color, label and drawing order. Part of the [`charts` extension](/docs/extension-charts): add `charts` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. With the next release, `tooltip:` (a text, or a hash with `text` and `text_style`) gives the spot a touch bubble; with 0.0.23 scatter charts show none. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-segment.summary: One option of a [`segmented_button`](/docs/control-segmented-button). `value` is required, and is what the button reports in `selected` and `on_change`; `label` and `icon` are what the user sees.
example: segment("grid", label: "Grid", icon: icon("grid_view"), tooltip: "Show a grid"),
segment("map", label: "Map", icon: icon("map"), disabled: true)

control-shadow.summary: A Material-style shadow cast by an outline, drawn before the shape that sits on it. It is drawn only inside a [`canvas`](/docs/control-canvas), in the order of its `shapes`; positions are logical pixels from the canvas's top-left corner. It is core Ruflet, no extension needed, and looks the same on every platform.

control-simple-attribution.summary: A small badge in a corner of the map that credits the tile provider, as most providers require. On iOS and macOS it is a Cupertino button whose text starts with "flutter_map |" and a copyright sign; elsewhere it shows just your text. Put it last in the map's `layers`. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-slide-picker.summary: Picks a color with one slider per channel, in RGB, HSV or HSL, with an optional preview bar. iOS and macOS draw it with Cupertino-styled sliders. Part of the [`color_pickers` extension](/docs/extension-color-pickers): add `color_pickers` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client. On 0.0.23 the sliders jump back to `color` whenever the picker is rebuilt, for example when you update one of its properties (pass the last pick from `event.data` as `color:` in that update), and a tap on the preview bar picks `color` again. The next release keeps the pick itself, but `event.control.props["color"]` still does not follow it, so read the pick from `event.data`. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-snack-bar-action.summary: The styled action button of a [`snack_bar`](/docs/control-snack-bar): `snack_bar_action(label, on_click:)`, passed as the snack bar's `action:`. Its own `on_click` fires when it is tapped. It is never drawn on its own, so its common layout properties have no effect. On Android, web, Windows and Linux `text_color` and `bgcolor` color the button, `disabled_text_color` and `disabled_bgcolor` color it once it has been pressed, and tapping it closes the snack bar. On iOS and macOS it is a plain iOS button that leaves the snack bar open; there `disabled: true` turns it off.

control-table-row.summary: One row of a [`table`](/docs/control-table): `table_row(cells, bgcolor:)`, with the cells as the first argument, as `controls:` or in a block, and `bgcolor` filling the row. Every row of a `table` must be a `table_row`. A row with fewer cells than the widest row is padded with empty cells, and a hidden cell keeps its column.

control-text-source-attribution.summary: One text line in a [`rich_attribution`](/docs/control-rich-attribution) popup, such as the name of a data source. It is drawn only there. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
example: text_source_attribution("Data: city open data portal", prepend_copyright: false)

control-tile-layer.summary: The base imagery of a [`map`](/docs/control-map), loaded as tiles from a server such as OpenStreetMap. Put it first in `layers`, set `user_agent_package_name` to your app id, and respect the provider's usage policy and attribution rules. Part of the [`map` extension](/docs/extension-map): add `map` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.

control-video.summary: A video player with a playlist, drawn with media_kit. It shows playback controls (Cupertino-style on iOS and macOS, Material elsewhere) unless `show_controls` is false, and methods such as `play_or_pause`, `seek` and `next` control it from Ruby once it is on the page. Most settings, the playlist included, are read when the player is created. Part of the [`video` extension](/docs/extension-video): add `video` under `extensions:` in `ruflet.yaml` and rebuild the client.
